relevance_note: Single-centre case series of 11 patients with genetically confirmed Blau syndrome, each tabulated individually: 'All patients in our cohort had the R334W variant in NOD2 gene.'
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON from my reading, and spans for Table 1 cells are the row prefix from the patient number through the cell (checked verbatim by script). Labels: Table 1 has a 'Patient no.' column of bare numbers; patients the text names ('patient no. N') are labelled 'patient no. N', while patients 2 and 6, never named in the text, are 'Table 1 #2' and 'Table 1 #6'. Table 1 ages are recorded as printed (unit 'years' from the column header); values such as 2.10, 9.11, 6.11 and 8.11 suggest a years.months notation while the delay column looks decimal, so ISO durations are given only for whole-number ages and left null otherwise. Variant: the paper prints only the protein change (R334W; p.R334W in the Figure 3 legend) and states 'missense heterozygous' for all patients; no transcript or cDNA. Inheritance: the six affected parents (Table 1 family history: father of #2, mother of 3, father of 4, mother of 7 and 8, father of 9, mother of 10) are covered by 'Affected symptomatic parents were also found to have the same mutation', so their children are recorded as inherited maternal/paternal; 'The mutation was de novo in four children' names no one, so no child is recorded de novo (sporadic patients 1, 5, 6, 11 left not reported). Parents' own variant rows carry no zygosity or type. Relatives: the asymptomatic carrier brother of patient no. 4 (R334W, 25 years) has no phenotype rows ('asymptomatic' excludes nothing specific); the 'elder sister of patient no. 7' in Figure 1D is kept as a separate person although she may be patient no. 8 (female sibling of pt. 7); this is not stated. 'Other features: No' in Table 1 was not used to exclude fever or other items (whole-category negative). 'Rash: No' (a word, not a symbol) was taken as excluded. Contradictions: (1) Table 1 calls patient no. 4 'cousin of pt. 3' but the Figure 2 legend calls patients 3 and 4 'siblings' (they have different affected parents); (2) patient no. 3 has 'Rash: No' in Table 1 but the Discussion says he was diagnosed with sJIA because of 'fever, rash, arthritis' - both rows emitted, checklist rash not reported; (3) text says camptodactyly in seven patients but Table 1 lists it for eight (1,2,3,5,6,7,8,9); (4) Introduction says 'nine families', Results '10 families'; (5) text says six patients were initially diagnosed as non-BS including 'early-onset sarcoidosis (n = 1 adult)', but Table 1 lists six with initial diagnosis 'BS' and none as EOS; (6) 'seven parents who carried the mutation' vs six affected parents; (7) patient no. 7's death is attributed to tubercular meningitis in Results but the Discussion says renal involvement 'was the cause of death in one child'; cause_of_death recorded as tubercular meningitis; (8) the 'all patients' statement of elevated ESR and CRP sits beside Table 1 values for patient no. 5 (ESR 12, CRP 1.87) with no stated reference ranges. Patient no. 5 was previously reported (ref 8). Unnamed counts (e.g. adalimumab stopped in one patient for TB reactivation; retinal vasculitis in two eyes) were not assigned to anyone.
